description: Amonix Space is an engineering and orbital mechanics team developing "Amonix Helios," an interactive navigation tool for lunar south pole landing missions. Using NASA LRO elevation datasets (LOLA) and planetary ephemeris calculations, we analyze Sun and Earth visibility angles to optimize solar power generation and direct-to-Earth communications for future Artemis missions.
summary: Amonix Helios is an autonomous Lunar South Pole mission planning, 3D rover escape trajectory, and ISRU water-ice propellant engine built for Artemis III. At the Lunar South Pole, low solar elevation (1.5°) and rugged crater rims create 15-day continuous darkness and -180°C temperatures that freeze static landers. By fusing real NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data with LRO LOLA DEM topography, Amonix Helios optimizes vertical solar arrays (22 m²), a 280 kWh battery bank, and a 360 W Lunar Night Hibernation mode alongside a 14.18 km sun-chasing rover escape path—cutting 1,510 kg in payload mass and saving $1.81B in NASA CLPS launch costs.
details:
1. Amonix Helios is an end-to-end physics, orbital mechanics, and mission architecture decision-support engine built for Artemis III Lunar South Pole operations (Challenge: Lunar Landing Site Navigator).

What It Does & How It Works: Using real NASA JPL Horizons hourly ephemeris telemetry (Sun and Earth azimuth/elevation vectors) and LRO LOLA DEM topographic elevation models, the engine simulates solar illumination, Earth Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight, and radiative thermal decay across candidate landing sites including Shackleton Crater Rim, Malapert Massif, Connecting Ridge, and de Gerlache Rim.

Key Engineering Innovations:

  1. 3D LOLA Topographic Mesh & Sun-Chasing Rover Escape: Computes an optimal 14.18 km traverse path consuming only 12.05 kWh to move from shadowed regions to Sun-Haven peaks before eclipse onset, keeping battery State of Charge (SoC) safely above 20%.
  2. Vertical Solar Array & Night Hibernation: Models 90-degree vertical solar arrays (22 m²) to maximize low-horizon solar capture and prevent lunar regolith dust accumulation, paired with a 360 W Lunar Night Hibernation protocol that keeps avionics above -10°C across 30 days.
  3. Pareto Mass & Cost Optimization: Sizes the power subsystem at 1,890 kg (280 kWh battery + 22 m² array) versus 3,400 kg for static survival baselines, saving 1,510 kg and $1.81 Billion in launch costs at NASA CLPS pricing benchmarks.
  4. 360° Polar Skyplot & Relay Sizing: Identifies terrain-induced DTE communication blackouts and calculates the minimum orbital altitude required for a lunar relay orbiter.
  5. ISRU Propellant & Trade-Off Matrix: Computes safe daytime excavation windows in Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) yielding 114.9 kg of water ice (101.1 kg LOX/LH2 propellant) and ranks landing sites with one-click CSV telemetry export.

Tools, Languages & Repositories: Built with Python, Streamlit, Plotly (3D WebGL & Polar Charts), NumPy, and Pandas.
